reply:
That's not how it works. The reflog is local to each person's repository—it doesn't sync across developers. When you force push, you rewrite the remote history. The other two pull your new commits, but their local branches still point to the old commits that no longer exist on the remote. On their next pull, git doesn't "merge them back in"—it sees their branch as diverged from origin and they either get a merge conflict, have to manually rebase, or end up with a tangled history.

The cost: Two developers stuck fixing their branches manually when it should have been one conversation and a `--force-with-lease` (or just a regular push if the rebase was local-only).

Tell them first. If they haven't pushed yet, they rebase on top of your new history and there's no problem. If they have, one of you rebases on the other's work.
